sections.content: Myrtle Beach, South Carolina has quietly become one of the most investor-friendly markets on the East Coast. With over 17 million visitors per year, a booming retirement population, and a steady stream of relocating families, the demand for housing here is not slowing down. Whether you are brand new to investing or a seasoned pro looking to expand your portfolio, finding real estate deals in Myrtle Beach SC can be a smart move in 2024. If you are just getting started, check out our full Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide before diving in.
Myrtle Beach Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

The Grand Strand area, which stretches roughly 60 miles of coastline and includes Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, and Conway, has seen consistent population growth for the past decade. Horry County added more than 40,000 residents between 2020 and 2023, making it one of the fastest-growing counties in the entire country. That kind of population growth fuels housing demand, which is exactly what real estate investors need to see.

As of mid-2024, the median home price in the Myrtle Beach metro area sits around $310,000, though prices vary significantly by zip code and property type. Condos near the oceanfront can run anywhere from $150,000 to over $500,000, while single-family homes in suburban neighborhoods like Carolina Forest and Socastee hover between $250,000 and $380,000. Distressed properties and off-market deals can still be found well below market value, which is where the real opportunity lies for investors.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Myrtle Beach
Conway and the Inland Communities

Conway, located about 15 miles inland from the beach, is one of the most underrated spots for real estate investors right now. Home prices average around $220,000 to $260,000, and the town is seeing major growth as buyers get priced out of the beach corridor. For wholesalers and flippers, Conway offers a steady pipeline of older homes that need work, with strong resale demand from first-time buyers and retirees. Rental demand is also growing as workers in the tourism and healthcare sectors look for affordable housing close to their jobs.
Carolina Forest

Carolina Forest is a master-planned community just west of Myrtle Beach that has exploded in popularity. With newer construction, top-rated schools, and easy access to Highway 501, this area attracts families relocating from more expensive markets like Charlotte and Raleigh. Rental rates for single-family homes here typically run $1,600 to $2,200 per month, making it a solid long-term rental play. Flippers targeting this neighborhood need properties at 70 cents on the dollar or better to hit their numbers.
Socastee and Forestbrook

Socastee and the Forestbrook area offer some of the best value in the entire Grand Strand. These neighborhoods sit between Myrtle Beach and Conway and offer lower entry prices with strong rental demand. Investors can often find single-family rentals in the $240,000 to $280,000 range that rent for $1,500 to $1,800 per month. That math works a lot better than trying to squeeze cash flow out of a beachfront condo.

Pro Tip: Focus your deal-finding efforts within a 20-mile radius of the beach. Properties just outside the tourist zone often offer better price-to-rent ratios while still benefiting from the region's population growth and job market.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Myrtle Beach
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is very active in the Myrtle Beach area. There is a large inventory of older homes built in the 1980s and 1990s that are starting to show their age, and many of these are owned by retirees or out-of-state heirs who want a fast, hassle-free sale. Assignment fees in this market typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 depending on the deal. To build a consistent pipeline of these opportunities, focus on off-market real estate deals through direct mail, driving for dollars, and probate leads. If you are new to the strategy, our Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide is a great starting point.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

The fix and flip market in Myrtle Beach is alive and well. The average gross profit on a flip in the Grand Strand area runs between $35,000 and $65,000, according to local investor reports, though results vary based on purchase price, renovation costs, and how well you read the resale market. Renovation costs in South Carolina are generally lower than in the Northeast, with labor costs running 10 to 20 percent below national averages. Make sure you are running accurate after-repair value estimates before you commit to any deal. Use our free ARV Calculator to quickly estimate what a renovated property could sell for in any Myrtle Beach neighborhood.
Short-Term and Long-Term Rentals

Myrtle Beach's tourism economy makes it one of the top short-term rental markets in the Southeast. Oceanfront condos can generate $30,000 to $60,000 per year in gross Airbnb revenue during peak season, though you need to account for high HOA fees, management costs, and seasonal vacancies. For more stable returns, long-term rentals in inland neighborhoods like Carolina Forest, Socastee, and Conway offer cap rates in the 5 to 7 percent range, which is solid for this region. The local rental vacancy rate sits at approximately 5.2 percent, well below the national average of around 6.6 percent.

"Myrtle Beach is not just a vacation destination anymore. It is a full-time home for hundreds of thousands of people, and that permanent population is what makes it such a compelling rental market for long-term investors." — Local real estate investor and Grand Strand landlord
Current Market Trends Shaping Deals in 2024

items: Population growth is outpacing new construction, creating upward pressure on rents and home values across Horry County.
Rising insurance costs along the coast are pushing some buyers inland, increasing demand in Conway and Socastee.
Interest rate sensitivity is creating more motivated sellers among homeowners who bought at low rates and now need to move.
The short-term rental market is experiencing higher competition, which is pushing savvy investors toward long-term rental strategies for more predictable income.
New infrastructure investments, including road expansions on Highway 31 and Route 9, are opening up new corridors for residential development and increasing property values in adjacent neighborhoods.
Foreclosure filings in Horry County have ticked up slightly in 2024 compared to 2023, which may create more distressed inventory for investors over the next 12 to 18 months.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Investing remotely in Myrtle Beach is very doable, but it requires building the right team on the ground. Start with a local real estate agent who works specifically with investors and understands ARVs and rental comps, not just retail sales. You will also need a reliable property manager if you plan to hold rentals, and at least two or three licensed contractors you can trust for accurate renovation bids. South Carolina does not have a state income tax on earned income, but it does have property taxes, so make sure you understand how the county assesses investment properties versus primary residences.

Before you make an offer on any deal, run the numbers carefully. Knowing how to analyze real estate deals like a pro is the single most important skill you can develop as an out-of-state investor. Use our free Deal Calculator to quickly model wholesale assignments, flips, and rental scenarios so you never overpay for a property. You can also explore active investment opportunities and market data for this area directly on our Myrtle Beach SC market page.

items: Visit the market at least once before closing your first deal. Walk neighborhoods, talk to locals, and get a feel for which areas are improving and which are stagnant.
Join local REIA (Real Estate Investor Association) meetings in Horry County or Myrtle Beach. These are goldmines for finding deal flow, contractor referrals, and joint venture partners.
Study the micro-markets. A street in North Myrtle Beach can have a completely different rental demand profile than one two miles away in Atlantic Beach.

Account for hurricane and flood insurance costs in your deal analysis. Coastal properties can carry insurance premiums of $3,000 to $8,000 per year, which significantly affects your cash flow projections.
Use skip tracing and direct mail to reach distressed property owners who may not be listing on the MLS. Many of the best deals in Myrtle Beach never hit the open market.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Pull Horry County tax delinquency lists and probate court records. These two sources consistently produce some of the most motivated sellers in the Myrtle Beach market, and most investors overlook them entirely.
Is Myrtle Beach Right for You?

Myrtle Beach is not a get-rich-quick market, but it is a get-rich-steady market if you are patient and disciplined. The combination of tourism, retirement migration, and family relocation creates multiple overlapping demand drivers that most markets simply do not have. Whether you are looking to wholesale a few deals per month, flip properties for profit, or build a long-term rental portfolio, there is room for a focused investor to succeed here in 2024 and beyond. The key is knowing your numbers, building the right local team, and being selective about which deals you pursue.
